title: The Declaration of Independence
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 1). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: What founding document said the American colonies were free from Britain?
facts: Long ago, the American colonies were ruled by Britain.
Over time, the colonists became angry. Britain made them pay high taxes, but they had no vote in Britain's government. British soldiers even stayed in their homes.
Many colonists had come to America for freedom, including religious freedom. They wanted to govern themselves.
On July 4, 1776, the Declaration of Independence said the colonies were free from Britain. We remember this day on Independence Day.
It also says all people are created equal and have rights that no one can take away.

newWords.meaning: a place ruled by a country far away
an important statement made in public
being free from another country's control

story.say: Long ago, the American colonies were ruled by Britain.

help.simpler: Before the United States existed, Britain controlled these lands. They were called colonies.
help.example: There were 13 colonies along the Atlantic coast, like Virginia, Massachusetts and New York.
help.why: This is where the story of the United States begins: the colonies later chose to be free.

story.say: Over time, the colonists became angry. Britain made them pay high taxes, but they had no vote in Britain’s government.

help.simpler: Britain took tax money from the colonists, but the colonists had no say in the rules.
help.example: In 1765, Britain taxed newspapers and other papers in the colonies. The colonists never got a vote on it.
help.why: “No taxation without representation” was a big reason the colonists wanted to be free.

check.statement: The colonists had a vote in Britain’s government.

story.say: British soldiers even stayed in their homes.

help.simpler: The colonists sometimes had to let British soldiers live in their houses.
help.example: A family might have to give soldiers a place to sleep, even if they did not want to.
help.why: This is one reason the colonists felt they had lost control over their own lives.

story.say: Many colonists had come to America for freedom, including religious freedom. They wanted to govern themselves.

help.simpler: Many people came to America to be free and to pray in their own way. They wanted to make their own rules.
help.example: The Pilgrims came in 1620 so they could practice their religion freely.
help.why: Freedom and self-government are big ideas in American history and on the civics test.

check.prompt: What did many colonists come to America for?

story.say: On July 4, 1776, the Declaration of Independence said the colonies were free from Britain.

help.simpler: On July 4, 1776, the colonies said: we are free from Britain. They wrote it in the Declaration of Independence.
help.example: “Declaration” means an important statement made in public. “Independence” means being free from another country’s control.
help.why: The test asks which founding document said the colonies were free from Britain.

story.say: We remember this day on Independence Day.

help.simpler: Every year on July 4, Americans remember the day the Declaration was adopted.
help.example: Many people celebrate with fireworks, parades and family picnics.
help.why: Independence Day is a national holiday. It reminds Americans when the country said it was free.

story.say: The Declaration also says all people are created equal and have rights that no one can take away.

help.simpler: Every person has the same worth. Some rights belong to everyone, and no one can take them away.
help.example: The Declaration names some of these rights: life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.
help.why: The test asks why the Declaration is important. “It says all people are created equal” is one answer.

check.prompt: What does the Declaration say about all people?
Tap the document that said the colonies were free from Britain.

listen.explanationKey: The words “Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness” are in what founding document?
facts: “Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness” are words from the Declaration of Independence.
The pursuit of Happiness means the freedom to try to make a good life.

story.say: “Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness” are words from the Declaration of Independence.

help.simpler: These famous words come from the Declaration of Independence, written in 1776.
help.example: Life means the right to live. Liberty means freedom. The pursuit of Happiness means trying to build a good life.
help.why: The test asks which document has these words. The answer is the Declaration of Independence.

help.simpler: Liberty and freedom mean the same thing.
help.example: Liberty is being free to speak, to pray and to live your life your way, within the law.
help.why: Liberty is one of the big ideas of the Declaration and the Constitution.

story.say: The pursuit of Happiness means the freedom to try to make a good life.

help.simpler: “Pursuit” means trying to reach something. You are free to try to build a happy life.
help.example: Choosing your own job, learning new things or starting a family are ways to pursue happiness.
help.why: It means the government should not stop you from trying to build a good life.

check.prompt: Tap the document with the words “Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness.”

readIt.sentence: Why do people come to the United States?
